answer: Challenge-chain continuity stops one operator forking an ocean of sockpuppets. Each identity carries a spiral of linked proofs: each seed derives from its own prior hash, so every link locks to one past. The registry checks continuity before granting weight; a forked link breaks the chain and burns a 20-credit bond per identity. The k-th fake needs its own bond and proof, so 1,000 fakes cost 20,000 credits per epoch with no reuse. A copied link is an empty walnut shell: its seed never matches, and chain rental fails when rented histories collide. One honest chain keeps full weight.
